newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips mostly up, SAX index firms.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips mostly up, SAX index firms.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mostly higher in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, with brokers predicting further growth for the market over the longer-term.

Slovnaft, the most heavily-weighted issue on the 16-share SAX index, closed up six crowns at 856. Its average price, used for calculating the index, rose 3.39 percent helping boost the index by 2.5 points to 193.4.
Dealers said they were bullish mainly due to the growth potential of several blue chips, such as steel maker VSZ, Slovnaft and bank VUB, which are still the main targets for foreign investors.
"Though there may be downward corection within some two weeks, from the longer-term perspective we see the market rising further," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Brokers said they expect Slovnaft to rise further given its higher price on the o-t-c market, a possible indication that investors are willing to accept higher prices to fulfil their demands.

VSZ gained 10 crowns and closed at 680. Sykora said it remained one of the most liquid issues, but added that the shareholders still seemed to be waiting to sell at higher prices which should push the share further up.
"Given the demand for VSZ shares and the reluctancy of sellers, it may well rise up to around 700 crowns," he said.
VUB bank was the biggest net winner at the day's session, rising 34 crowns to 1,750, but traded only 29 shares - too little to indicate long-term, brokers said.
Overall volume fell to 239,048 shares, from 763,984 stock traded on Monday, while turnover decreased to 281.95 million, from 837.56 million.
